hypotheses.claim: Observational/differential equivalence of H1/H2/H3 is insufficient for causal-emergence comparison unless each declared semantic intervention is shown to commute with implementation-specific lowering/projection.
hypotheses.mechanism: Physical/module fusion can mix semantic variables. A low-level clamp that was a one-variable lesion in H1 may alter several semantic variables in H3 even when unlesioned trajectories are equivalent.
hypotheses.prediction: There exist semantically equivalent implementations with near-zero baseline divergence but materially different lesion/rescue effects under naive coordinate-level interventions.
hypotheses.falsifier: Across a broad corpus of representation changes and H1/H2/H3 interventions, naive implementation-local lesions yield the same semantic counterfactual trajectories/effects as explicitly mapped semantic interventions within preregistered tolerance.

hypotheses.claim: A versioned semantic-intervention lowering receipt can turn cross-implementation lesion/rescue into a translation-validation problem rather than an informal module-name match.
hypotheses.mechanism: Bind semantic intervention identity to a lowering map, implementation hash, semantic projection, expected collateral write set and counterfactual commutation error.
hypotheses.prediction: Correctly mapped interventions preserve semantic counterfactual traces/effect estimates across equivalent implementations while malformed mappings fail the commutation check.
hypotheses.falsifier: The receipt/check cannot distinguish deliberately wrong low-level targets from correct targets, or its false-negative/false-positive rate is unacceptable on seeded benchmark transformations.

hypotheses.claim: H3 one-module/fused lowering is the highest-risk stage for intervention aliasing because logical causal variables may cease to correspond to physical process/module coordinates.
hypotheses.mechanism: Consolidation preserves logical planes while changing physical topology; one semantic lesion may require a distributed low-level mechanism transformation rather than zeroing one component.
hypotheses.prediction: Intervention maps that are trivial in H1 become multi-target or transformed operations in at least some H3 candidates while semantic effect remains invariant under the correct map.
hypotheses.falsifier: The actual H3 representation preserves a stable one-to-one intervention address for every mandatory H1 causal handle without hidden collateral effects.

counterhypotheses.claim: Existing ClayCode typed intervention/state semantics plus ordinary H1/H2/H3 differential replay are already sufficient; no new semantic primitive is required.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Compile a representative SemanticIntervention + LoweringReceipt fixture through the current BASE parser/IR/type-effect/evaluator. A language change is warranted only on an executable representability/lowering failure.

counterhypotheses.claim: End-to-end semantic trace equivalence under the mandatory intervention corpus is sufficient even without an explicit abstraction/lowering map.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Seed malformed low-level interventions that accidentally match selected output metrics but alter hidden semantic state; test whether trace-only validation catches them reliably.

counterhypotheses.claim: Actual H3 consolidation will retain logical typed substates strongly enough that intervention aliasing is negligible in practice.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: When H3 exists, enumerate all mandatory intervention handles and measure target multiplicity, collateral semantic writes and commutation error against H1 Golden counterfactual traces.
